import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 75

*Reference:*
* [erdosproblems.com/75] (https://www.erdosproblems.com/75)
-/

open Cardinal

namespace Erdos75

/--
Is there a graph of chromatic number `ℵ_ 1` with `ℵ_ 1` vertices such that for all
`ε > 0`, if `n` is sufficiently large and `H` is a subgraph on `n` vertices,
then `H` contains an independent set of size `> n ^ (1 - ε)`?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_75 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V),
      G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 ∧
      #V = ℵ_ 1 ∧
      ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ),
        ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∀ (H : G.Subgraph),
            H.verts.ncard = n →
            ∃ (I : Finset V),
              (I : Set V) ⊆ H.verts ∧
              G.IsIndepSet (I : Set V) ∧
              (I.card : ℝ) > (n : ℝ) ^ (1 - ε) := by
  sorry

end Erdos75

reformulations.difference: Lean requires the independent set to be independent in G, rather than only in H, and uses H.verts.ncard = n without an explicit finiteness hypothesis.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Independence in G implies independence in any subgraph H. Conversely, apply the source condition to the induced subgraph of G on H.verts: its independent sets are independent in G, and it has the same vertex count as H. Thus the universally quantified requirements are equivalent. Moreover, eventually n ≥ 2; for positive n, H.verts.ncard = n forces H.verts to be finite, since infinite sets have ncard zero. Filter.atTop supplies precisely a threshold N(ε) uniform over all H. The complete RHS equivalence, with explicit finite subgraphs, intrinsic independence, and a threshold N ≥ 2, was proved as Review75.full_rhs_iff_literal_source in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: The sole declaration faithfully states the source's n^(1−ε) existence question; the page still marks it open. Checked answer scope, both cardinal equalities, real exponentiation, and empty/singleton cases. Lean proofs also verify that chromaticCardinal is an attained minimum and that graphs with the prescribed vertex cardinality have subgraphs of every finite order, so the universal condition is not vacuous.
